title: Graceful cold-start deprioritization and progressive warmup for Dedicated fleets
creator: Samir Patel
description: Goal: reduce cold-start tail latencies and eliminate noisy spikes when tenants are routed to Dedicated capacity. Approach: implement a deprioritization admission controller that intentionally slows or staggers non-critical cold starts while running a progressive warmup pipeline that streams weight slices and performs lightweight KV cache probing in the background. This ticket covers the controller design, policy DSL, telemetry hooks, and validation in staging clusters.
acceptance_criteria: P90 cold-start latency for newly allocated worker pods reduces by >= 40% under mixed traffic compared to current baseline
System maintains dedicated throughput guarantees (per-tenant qps SLA) while warmup progresses for new workers
KV cache hit-rate for primed prefixes increases by at least 30% within the first 60s of warmup
Feature is controllable via fleet config flags and can be toggled per-tenant for canary rollouts
Comprehensive dashboards added: warmup_progress, deprioritized_requests, staged_weight_streaming_bytes, kv_probe_success_rate
tasks: Design admission controller policy DSL and backpressure semantics
Implement progressive weight streamer with prioritization tiers (metadata, embeddings, attention matrices)
Add lightweight KV probe agent integrated with prefix-sampling table
Expose warmup metrics to Console and add per-route visualization
Write e2e test harness simulating bursty tenant onboarding and traffic handoff
Create rollout runbook and automated rollback on error budget breaches
notes: We deliberately separate deprioritization (short-term request shaping) from slow-path warmup (background streaming) to avoid request-level timeouts.
Progressive streamer will prefer read-mostly slices first (embeddings/kv-friendly layers) and defer large weight blocks until baseline throughput stabilizes.
Admission controller will tag low-priority requests with a tracing marker so Console can surface impact and allow PM to tune thresholds.
Expect interactions with Dedicated autoscaler: autoscaler should consult warmup state to avoid scaling loops (i.e., don't scale up for deprioritized requests).
risks: If streamer saturates network links during large fleet onboarding, it could impact sustained throughput for other tenants
Incorrect deprioritization thresholds could cause visible throttling for latency-sensitive customers
KV probe false positives could lead to overconfident routing decisions if probes are not representative of real prefixes
mitigations: Add token-bucket shaping to weight streamer and backpressure signals to pause streaming when per-host tx bytes > threshold
Start with conservative deprioritization parameters and conduct staged canaries on low-impact tenants
Use statistical prefix sampling and validate probe patterns against historical traces before enabling for a tenant
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and admission controller decision tree
Integration tests: simulate tenant cold-start with synthetic load and measure latencies and kv hit-rate
Chaos test: inject streaming pauses and ensure fallback to cold-path is safe and observable
Load test in dedicated staging cluster to validate throughput guarantees under concurrent warmups
rollout_plan: Phase A: Internal canary - enable for platform-internal tenants only (1% of traffic)
Phase B: Selected customers - opt-in via account feature flag; monitor error budgets and dashboards
Phase C: Gradual broader rollout with automated tuning rules for deprioritization thresholds
Emergency rollback: global toggle to disable admission controller and cancel active streamers
